sql:
SELECT z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone, COUNT(t.PULocationID) AS cash_trips
FROM ops.zones z
LEFT JOIN lake.trips t ON t.PULocationID = z.LocationID AND t.payment_type = 2
GROUP BY z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone
ORDER BY z.LocationID

diagnosis.bottleneck: The hash join (node 8) forces a CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) on the probe side for ~99K filtered trips rows, preventing predicate pushdown and adding per-row conversion cost; the join then feeds 99K rows into a hash aggregation that only produces 265 groups.

plan_nodes.note: Join Type: RIGHT | Conditions: CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) = LocationID | Estimated Cardinality: 99167

hypotheses.claim: A filter on the joined side sits in the ON clause of a LEFT JOIN; the join dominates the cost. (matched: left join lake.trips t on … and t.payment_type = 2)

The CAST in the join condition (CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) = LocationID) disables join-key partition pruning and forces a type conversion on every probe row; removing the cast or aligning column types would allow a faster hash join.

The hash join builds on the larger filtered trips input (~99K rows) instead of the tiny zones table (265 rows); forcing a build on zones (e.g., via join order hint or rewriting as aggregated subquery) would shrink the hash table and reduce probe cost.

The HASH_GROUP_BY processes 99K rows to produce only 265 groups; pre-aggregating trips by PULocationID + payment_type before the join would reduce the join input cardinality by ~400x and eliminate the post-join aggregation.
